claims.text: Market equilibrium is the position of a market in which the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied; the price at which the two are equal is the equilibrium price, and the quantity bought and sold at that price is the equilibrium quantity.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: At the equilibrium price the market clears: buyers take the quantity sellers offer, no stock is left unsold and no would-be buyer goes without, so the price tends to stay where it is until demand or supply changes.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: The equilibrium is found by reading a demand schedule against a supply schedule, price by price, until the two quantities match, or on a diagram by marking where the demand curve crosses the supply curve, with price on the vertical axis and quantity on the horizontal.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A change in demand or supply carries the market to a new equilibrium: a rise in demand tends to raise the equilibrium price and the equilibrium quantity, while a rise in supply tends to raise the equilibrium quantity and lower the equilibrium price.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: Market disequilibrium is a position of a market in which the quantity demanded does not equal the quantity supplied at the prevailing price, which happens where the price sits above or below its equilibrium level.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A surplus exists where the price sits above its equilibrium level, so the quantity supplied exceeds the quantity demanded, and a shortage exists where the price sits below it, so the quantity demanded exceeds the quantity supplied.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: Out of equilibrium the price comes under pressure: a surplus tends to push the price down as sellers cut prices to clear unsold stock, and a shortage tends to push the price up as buyers who miss out offer more, so the market tends to move back towards equilibrium.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: At the Swakopmund weekend market the equilibrium price of a woven basket is N$45; when a trader holds the price at N$60, the quantity demanded is 60 baskets and the quantity offered is 90, a surplus of 30 baskets, since 90 - 60 = 30 baskets.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.
